normative_summary: Rendering owns Evaluation Capability contracts.
Each exact Expression Profile permanently maps to exact capability contracts.
expression/1.0 maps only CLOCK and RANDOM to their frozen v1 contracts.
Template, use, request, and deployment cannot add, replace, mask, or negotiate capability contracts.
Capability ValueSource has exactly three frozen closed wire shapes and typed outputs.
Capability wire forbids args, seed, timezone, contractVersion, latest, null, and unknown members.
Capability source is legal only as an explicit ExpressionDefinition input; source reads it through input alias.
Capability is not a function, schema, system map, or general ValueSource and is forbidden in Binding, Mapping, default, fill, structure, and property.
Save or recheck statically validates every authored closure capability source, including unused, unselected, and unreachable sources.
An illegal capability contract is a non-confirmable hard error.
Admitted Profile support is permanent and capability declarations create no Asset-style reverse index or STALE propagation.
CapabilityState creation occurs only after closure, profile, input, dynamic-Asset, and authored-dependency admissions succeed.
Any earlier failure performs zero Clock or entropy read.
CapabilityState commits before the root invocation frame.
Static scan covers all declared contracts in the complete closure, including unreachable or uninvoked sources.
Any CLOCK declaration creates one Clock snapshot; any RANDOM declaration creates one nonce.
An undeclared component is not created; no capability source means no state record.
Deployment must nevertheless fully support every admitted Expression Profile.
One root Evaluation has one CapabilityState shared across actual child invocations and related output commands.
A different RootDocument, root Template, or batch record requires a distinct Evaluation state.
Rendering creates an internal renderRequestId; the caller cannot select the state key.
Future public retry can resume only through an authorized server mapping or handle for the same fingerprint.
Retry identity cannot select time or nonce or reuse state for another request.
Clock reads one UTC instant during state linearization and truncates toward the past whole second.
Clock domain is proleptic Gregorian year 1 through 9999 and whole-day time range, without leap seconds.
Provider error or out-of-range Clock result fails the request.
UTC_DATE and UTC_TIME project canonical date and time from the same snapshot without midnight mixing.
Different aliases or frames remain distinct budgeted and digested call positions even if values match.
Clock is UTC-only and reads no server, browser, tenant, or actor timezone.
Business-local time must enter as RootDocument or Custom input.
Clock exposes no datetime, instant, epoch, offset, timezone, or text.
Expression Clock is isolated from deadline, timeout, latency, and expiry clocks.
Wall-clock changes after snapshot do not change the value; operation timing never enters Expression.
Random state uses exactly a 256-bit server-only nonce from a trusted OS CSPRNG.
Nonce is request-derivation-only and excluded from all authored, public, log, problem, document, cache, and history surfaces.
Random output has no token, identity, or security-random guarantee.
CallPosition binds the Definition declaration frame, not a consumer Node.
CallPosition path includes exact root, use, and repeat declaration segments plus definition, alias, contract, and operation.
An invocation-domain Definition excludes downstream consumer loops and memoizes across them.
A loop-domain Definition derives independently per original input item.
Duplicate items stay distinct and reorder changes item-to-random association.
Derivation never uses item content, business key, final occurrence, or call ordinal.
CallPosition semantic object has the exact closed six-field v1 shape.
Path begins with exactly one ROOT and then only frozen TEMPLATE_USE or REPEAT segment shapes.
Path ends at declaration domain; all strings are required and revision and index are nonnegative integers.
positionBytes uses frozen canonical member, string, and integer rules and semantic path order.
CallPosition has no normalization, set sorting, unknown, optional, or null fields; exact byte vectors are permanent conformance.
Random HMAC input, domain, length framing, counter, and unsigned digest interpretation are exact.
Random uses M equal to 10^18 rejection sampling over counters 0 through 127.
One hundred twenty-eight rejected samples return CAPABILITY_RESULT_INVALID.
Uniform output domain is exactly k over 10^18 including zero and the specified maximum.
Random result is exact BigDecimal with trailing-zero semantics.
Typed encoding is independent of binary float, locale, and object stringification.
Capability demand occurs only when lazy Expression evaluation actually reads the input alias.
An unmaterialized Definition or unselected branch creates zero demand while remaining statically validated.
First demand of a CallPosition computes its unique result.
Same-expression alias reread and same-frame Definition memo hit do not call or recount.
Different aliases are distinct positions and budget entries; Random derivations differ.
Demand order follows the frozen argument, lazy, consumer, and frame order.
Evaluator serializes logical demands and stops on the first error.
Unobservable parallel preparation cannot change result, count, first error, or Asset order.
Capability ERROR is not ABSENT and cannot be swallowed by exists or coalesce.
The first demanded capability ERROR stops all later capability, Asset, lowering, and Engine work with no fallback or partial output.
First demand atomically reserves total and matching kind budget before producing a result.
Any budget excess produces no result and returns CAPABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
Alias or memo reread and state initialization do not consume demand units.
Physical Clock or HMAC reuse never reduces logical counts.
All capability count, byte, retry, expiry, and deadline limits are exact and fail closed.
Profile or deployment cannot per-caller or per-Template relax limits or create unversioned differences.
Clock and Random execute inside the trusted Evaluator with no network, file, plugin, Engine, or per-call fee.
Internal idempotency storage is infrastructure and not capability-visible I/O.
Cancel or total deadline yields zero RenderDocument and zero Output.
Deadline or state cannot extend, renew, become an Expression input, or be reused for a new request.
One linearized state operation reads required providers and commits an encrypted short-term record.
Record key and bound fingerprint, contracts, snapshot or nonce, and timestamps are exact.
The root frame starts only after record commit.
Evaluation fingerprint includes frozen scope, authorization, closure, input, contract, and budget fields.
Fingerprint excludes request id, state, results, Asset selection, URL, output, and timing.
Fingerprint and state record are not returned to the caller.
The same request and fingerprint replays committed state; a different fingerprint conflicts.
A precommit transient failure may bounded-retry; unknown commit queries the record first.
Postcommit never resamples.
A different requestId always creates new state even with the same fingerprint.
expiresAt is fixed at creation and covers render deadline plus retry margin.
Retry, cancel, or downstream failure never extends expiry.
Expired failure records are not audit, history, backup, or public-query objects.
Capability provider failures map only to the frozen stable request codes and safe parameters.
Unknown or invalid capability shape, type, or location is a non-confirmable DesignDSL hard error.
An admitted-profile provider or state transient failure affects the request only and creates no readiness or revision state.
Public errors expose a stable code and safe request locator only by default.
Authorized Template diagnostics may expose definition, alias, and bounded segment-authorized InvocationPath.
Unauthorized child path segments are redacted.
No layer exposes result, nonce, fingerprint, input, provider, stack, or raw error.
Successful Evaluation digests actual demanded results in encounter order with exact closed typed entry encoding.
Each entry is uint64-length framed and hashed with the frozen capability-results domain.
Undemanded state, nonce, unprojected Clock, physical execution, cache, and timing are excluded.
Capability and Asset result digests are distinct runtime components of complete Evaluation identity.
Content hash or capability declaration cannot replace actual result identity.
Downstream cache is allowed only after the full admission and Evaluation identity exists.
Successful metadata may persist only digest, contract IDs, aggregate counts, result code, and timing.
Failure produces no partial digest or transcript; only aggregate consumption, timing, and code may remain.
Call positions, snapshot, nonce, and typed results are never retained long term.
State, digest, handle, or cache cannot skip unproven recovery stages or become cross-request replay.
Evaluator writes only capability-affected concrete typed Node values.
RenderDocument, resources, and Engine contain no capability state, contract, path, digest, value, handle, or source label.
Engine cannot distinguish literal, context, or capability origin.
Every new authoritative preview creates a new Evaluation and state; only same-operation internal recovery replays.
v1 offers no EditorSession time or seed pin.
Draft simulation or placeholder is explicitly non-authoritative, nonpersistent, and cannot preserve old authority.
The editor picker exposes only three typed operations for the exact Profile and does not call them system data sources.
The editor exposes no seed, timezone, version, or free args and warns that previews vary and Random is non-security.
Fixed instant or nonce injection exists only at an internal conformance seam.
Conformance injection never appears in production protocol, content, metadata, or configuration.
Web validates authored shape only; runtime simulation is labeled non-authoritative.
Metrics use bounded contract, operation, and status labels and aggregate counts, timing, and failures only.
Logs and traces prohibit high-cardinality author identity, results, state, fingerprints, input, and provider raw errors.
Authorized location is available only through a bounded structured problem.
Capability cannot observe tenant, actor, request, authorization, credential, Connector, Asset, or environment facts.
Those facts may affect internal authorization or fingerprint only.
HMAC output promises distribution only, not unpredictability or security.
Expression cannot convert Random into UUID, token, or arbitrary bytes; product domains generate security identity.
Every future capability is explicit-input, closed typed, readonly, request-scoped, credentialless, target-closed, and side-effect-free.
A new contract freezes operation, payload, output, position, stability, errors, budgets, diagnostics, and conformance.
A new capability requires a new exact Expression Profile plus explicit migration and save.
Mixed supported Expression Profiles use their own exact capability contracts over shared base state.
CallPosition and HMAC domain include each contract ID; root cannot override child and child cannot negotiate or mask.
Network, paid, business-read, mutation, credential, or dynamic-tool features belong outside Evaluation Capability.
TOOL, plugin, and general wrappers are forbidden.
Conformance covers all listed Clock, Random exact-vector, identity, lazy, state, budget, deadline, digest, and document-residue cases.
Negative corpus hard-fails invalid capability shapes, locations, and caller state injection.
No Random declaration means an entropy failure is unobservable.
No frontend, serializer, migration, or Engine path can relax the closed capability contract.
Problems, logs, traces, and responses never leak results or internal state.
v1 excludes all listed extra time, random, system, tool, network, mutation, replay, fallback, and latest capabilities.
Ticket14 creates no product implementation or placeholder surfaces.
